_doc: WIKI-REDESIGN-1107 (supersedes WIKIREF-1022's MediaWiki Action API design). English Wikipedia as a REFERENCE-LIST portal only (owner 2026-11-07: "for Wikipedia, we shouldn't use its page contents. instead, only search for reference links to follow those for original sources"; owner 2026-10-22: portal only, never evidence). Read only by vera/wiki_ref_portal.py. Articles are found with ONE DuckDuckGo Lite site: query (the shared /ask instance); only https://<article_host>/wiki/<Title> main-namespace pages are requested, each only after vera.selective_fetch.robots_allowed allows it (default-deny). Nothing under /w/, /api/ or Special: is ever requested (en.wikipedia.org/robots.txt, User-agent: *, disallows them; read 2026-11-07, work/WIKI-REDESIGN-1107/design.md). From each page ONLY the COinS reference metadata (title, venue, DOI/PMID/arXiv/URL) is read; article prose is never read, stored, scored, logged or shown. Relevant references become ordinary acquisition candidates (scholarly id, or the ORIGINAL https URL with web.archive.org unwrapped (nested snapshots too; other archive mirrors dropped)) and pass every existing gate. OFF unless `enabled` is exactly true; ships OFF until the owner or an independent review turns it on. No key, no secret, no env read.
_calibration_note: max_articles 3 and max_refs 20 are kept from WIKIREF-1022 (planner priors, not decision thresholds: every decision gate is the unchanged acquisition gate). timeout_s 5 and max_response_bytes 4000000 are SAFETY limits: the two article pages read on 2026-11-07 were 389 kB and 1.51 MB (work/WIKI-REDESIGN-1107/calibration.txt). relevance.min_hits 2 is PROVISIONAL (a prior; NOT sufficient to enable the portal: a live shadow check of 'autoacq wikiref' counts and the downstream relevance-gate pass rate must come first). Measured on 2 real reference lists (37 and 331 COinS references) and 7 questions on 2026-11-07: min_hits 1 kept 16-17 references of an OFF-TOPIC article for a stellar question and 208 for a two-stem news question; min_hits 2 kept 4 and 7 on-topic references for two stellar questions, 0 for the off-topic article and the Bingley question, and 92 (then capped to max_refs) for a CRISPR question. Spread is wide and the sample tiny. What would change it: 'autoacq wikiref' relevant/candidates counts and the downstream relevance-gate pass rate of portal candidates over live questions.
user_agent: VERA-DAR-wiki-ref-portal/0.2 (non-commercial educational research assistant; reference-list discovery only; https://github.com/taggm-ghc/vera-dar)

query._note: r2: generic verbs (make, work, use, happen, mean, ...) added so they never count as content stems in relevance or the site: query.

relevance._note: Reference relevance uses only the reference's own COinS title and venue, never Wikipedia prose. cue_terms (news/time words) and 4-digit years are not question stems (LINKS-VERIFY-1107 finding 3). max_refs_scanned (500) is a SAFETY bound on COinS spans parsed per page (largest seen: 331).
